published.source: docs/PUBLIC_BENCHMARKS.md:380-394 (accuracy vs human label, no option shuffling)

notes: Records are exactly the ids in Nimble's committed subset manifest, converted by Nimble's own public_sources/aegis2.py; the selected records re-serialize to Nimble's dataset_sha256 (verified).

Option text is the criteria description only, in Nimble's key order; the key names are dropped (as in build_jeff.py / typed-decisions). Nimble's prompt (nimble/scoring/parallel_schema.py:95-101) and the Jev request ({key: description}, dataset_io.request_for) also showed the key name.
state and instructions are Nimble's input.state / decision.instructions unchanged; stage = Nimble domain.

noul -> two options [criteria["false"], criteria["true"]]: public_records.record_for (public_records.py:63-64) fixes that order and evaluate_pilot.py:29-30 (adapt_input) renders choices [False, True]. answer 2 = true. Jev was asked a native noul (P(true)); here every system gets the same two-option choice.
source_sha256 matches the HF refs/convert/parquet export, not the repository's own json/jsonl.gz on main; both convert to the same dataset_sha256.

The "true" option (Nimble's twelve unsafe categories) is 69 tokens by build.py's tokenizer, over OPTION_TOKEN_CAP 48: Julia refuses such items (unsupported, scored wrong) and Laya truncates. Kept verbatim; it is the maker's criterion.
Nimble dropped 1 over-length row(s) (Qwen3.5-9B tokenizer, 2,048 tokens) before selection; the id list already reflects that. Nothing is truncated here.
